- `writes_via.covers`: the word of the unit does not close tables, the word of a table does not close the unit.
- `writes_via.pass`: the right of the ticket's person is judged as before (`need` and `may` of the door): the word narrows the path, it does not replace the rights.
- `writes_via.refuse`: in a batch — a refusal of the whole batch, nothing written, `detail` names the number of the row.
- `writes_via.refuse`: journal — `access.denied {sub, reason: "writes via"}` (the gate contract «Subsystem of the check»).
- `writes_via.order`: for a batch — by step 3 of «batch» on each row of `writes`.

- `id.numeric`: a number is never used again; tombstones count; a number issued to a refused attempt is not returned.

- `id.numeric.recover`: the counter does not read or there is no row → the greatest number among the rows `<rows>/` (with tombstones) and the numbers in live claims + 1 — the issued number; the counter is rewritten whole with `n` = this number (the last issued).
- `id.numeric.recover`: the numbers of refused attempts leave no traces and after a recovery MAY come out again — the only exception from «never», journal `next_id.recovered {from, to}`.

Successful numbers are represented by saved rows/tombstones; the cleanup of done claims does not cancel that. An arbitrary loss of these rows is not covered by the recover formula.
Cleanup of a done claim uses a local monotonic age; after the memory is recovered a new observer counts the done claim as fresh and does not trust foreign wall clocks.
The term of a done claim does not extend done to 5xx or pending: their fate stays by N3.
A ceiling gives a refusal, not a truncation.
An empty name, a path separator, a dot, a percent, a space, a control or non-ASCII character do not represent the blob door of this lesson: a load refusal `refused:value` with the path of the field.
Other fields are not narrowed automatically by the restriction on the name of a blob field.

A manifest with any blob field of a unit does not declare unit.fields.bytes: a load refusal `refused:value` by P/02.1. Without blob the field bytes is permitted. This restriction keeps the full Unit in the answer of the upload; a renaming of the counter or a new shell is not introduced.

- `sweep.sweep`: after the writers are stopped, check the references again; remove the list with `cas` (a conflict — delete nothing); delete the objects.
- `sweep.sweep`: `put_blob` removes the digest with `cas`; this cancellation is a help to the marks, not a protection against a parallel deletion.
- `stamp`: `by` — the user of the write; `at` — the wall-clock seconds of this write; `made_at` — the wall-clock seconds of the first write of the row, an overwrite keeps it.

`ETag` is carried by the success answers that name one row: `GET` of a table row; `POST`, `PUT` of a unit and the bytes door; `DELETE` of a unit — the tombstone index; `POST` of a table; the doors of [chapter 6.6](06.6-console.norms.md) N2.1.

`If-Match` is read by `PUT` and `DELETE` of a unit, `POST /{rows}` with `unit.id` by a name (N3 «create» step 5a), `POST` and `DELETE` of a table, the write doors of chapter 6.6 N2.1.
The bytes door, the batch door (the condition of a row is `cas`) and the requests door do not read `If-Match`.
At `POST /{rows}` with `unit.id: numeric` the header is not read: the console issues the number, the condition has nothing to judge.
The value of `If-Match` does not enter the fingerprint of a claim (N3 «repeat memory»).
The `If-Match` condition is judged after the claim and on each re-read of the procedure.
- `row`: secrets — by the mask (chapter 6.2).

- `row`: the field is absent if there is no row, if it is a tombstone (`POST` over a tombstone) and if the caller would not pass `need` of reading this row (the gate and pass contract): a refusal does not give values past `view`.
- A done claim with `row` heavier than the store ceiling — the answer and the write go without `row`: the refusal is more important than a copy of the row, the client re-reads it itself.
A tombstone keeps all fields of the row (N3 «delete» step 2), hence also the field `about`; there is no separate row. So a reader finds the index of a removed part when its name is nowhere any more.

- Read only: `index` — the tombstone index, `id` — as a string, `revision` — `revision` of the tombstone, an integer, 0 — does not read: a creation over it writes `revision` + 1 (N3 «create» step 8), a chain of steps counts the next version from here; the list in ascending order of `id` (UTF-8 bytes); no such tombstones — `{deleted: []}`.

A subsystem whose reader relies on the tombstone index of a part does not declare `placement.unplaced.delete_after`, `placement.retire_when.delete_after`, `placement.ends` for the part: a removed tombstone would bring back a former version.
The subsystem is always named in the path, also the root one: `/testsub/next_id`.

- No row: `n` — by recover of N1.3, `index` — `""`. The number that recover issues, minus one: the greatest number among the rows `<rows>/` with tombstones and the numbers of live claims; nothing — 0. `n + 1` stays the next number, as with a row.
- The row does not read: `n` the same, `index` — its version (P/01.1 N3 «read»): a batch write with this `cas` replaces it.
- The counter door does not write the counter; there is no journal.
- Another method at the counter door — 405; `HEAD` — like `GET`.
The door is common, like `/drain`: it gets no subsystem prefix, names the rows by full keys, rows of different subsystems go together.
The feed uses long polling: each request passes the gate anew, so the rights are checked without a separate closing of a stream, and the answer is ordinary JSON.
- **Scope.** A table `service: true` and operations with `service: true` enter only the feed by a ticket (N1.6, «Filter» below); their messages do not come to people without a ticket.
- **Scope.** Membership rows (their change is carried by the folder row), the form `tables: [<t>]` (it has no doors), events, heartbeats and metrics do not enter: they have their own doors.
- **Number.** The number is compared only for equality; the client does not compute by it.
- **Number.** The number acts only at the console instance that issued it, and only for a person with the rights with which it was issued («Implementation decides» item 10).

- **Start of a subscription.** A message with `revision: 0` the client verifies by reading the row. Another message with `revision` not higher than the one read it drops: so an edit in the gap of the load is not lost and does not roll back what was read.
- **Start of a subscription.** A message `deleted` the client verifies by reading this row, because it has no `revision`, and the row could have been created anew before the read.

- **Output.** `position` — how far the output went, including through messages that the caller does not see: the next request does not look through them. There were no new messages — `position` equals `after`.
- **`at`**: redelivery gives the same `at`: the value is kept by the history, not by the clock of the redelivery.
The door is common, like `/drain`: it gets no subsystem prefix, names the rows by full keys, rows of different subsystems go together.
The door does not read `If-Match`: the condition of each row is its `cas`.

- The counter is not removed: `delete` on `<s>/next_id` — 400 `bad batch`.
- **Anchor row**. The rule is held only by the batch door: a part created by a single `POST` does not move the anchor.

- **Counter**. `n` is the greatest number of the rows being created, and all of them are greater than the read `n` (N1.3: `n` — the last issued, a number is not used again); otherwise 400 `bad_id`, `field` — `/writes/<number>/fields/n`.

A prepared done claim is checked by weight before the write, like step 8: over the store ceiling — 413 `row too large`, the write is not performed, to step 9.
The one who took over first looks at the target, then goes through the door procedure:
Other door continuations keep their own confirmation rules.
The target is looked at before `If-Match`: the condition judges foreign edits, not one's own write.
Checking the claim by a separate read before an unconditional write is not enough.
After a successful change of the claim the executor remembers the new version; a takeover always changes it.
The empty form of int equals 0, so a manifest with a weight field without a suitable default may require an explicit positive value at POST; the materialization rules of N1.2 stay common.
A number written into the claim before the death is not burnt.
At exceeding the ceiling of a service write the reserved number is not returned.

Without it the edit converges by `cas` of the read row, and a repeat of PUT is a new edit that raises `revision` again; with it the edit goes under a claim, a repeat gives the saved answer (N3 «repeat memory»).

The condition is judged after the claim: a repeat with the same key answers from memory, not with `412` of its own edit.
The comparison is on each re-read of the procedure (after a `cas` conflict — from step 3 again). No header — as before.

The claim is `<CONSOLE_ROOT>/idem/<key>`, as for the cluster doors of chapter 6.6.
Another fingerprint under the same key — 422 `key reused`.
`done` goes by the write of the batch, not by a separate one: otherwise a break between them would leave a written batch with `pending`.
The one who took over goes through the procedure anew, from step 5; a late batch of the former executor is refused by the `cas` of the claim.
The fingerprint of a batch with secrets is taken not by the mask.
The CAS of the row protects only the row.
A parallel deletion is excluded by the sweep admission below; the cancellation of a mark and the control read do not replace this admission.
In the exceptional window the other sweepers, including mark, are stopped.
A new observer of the list always waits 300 s.
New candidates get only into the next batch after the former one is emptied.
Deletion is not an automatic action of a live installation.
The results of a pass obtained before the stop are not used for sweep.
The order: `If-Match` out of form → 400; the claim; no row → 404; `If-Match` not equal to the version of the row → 412; the removal.
The tick runs also without subscribers, because a client keeps the number between requests.
The tick does not overlap itself.

About a key of the first tick the memory knows only the index. At its next change `revision` is not compared (without `{deleted: ""}`), while `labels` and `members` count as changed: an extra reset is safe.
A message about a folder row whose `members` differ from the memory, and its tombstone, the history marks for reset 5.
